messages:
Anna R: Heads up — found a tenant snapshot uploaded without CMK tags to our blobstore during restore drill. Not exposing data but KMS grants didn't match. Upload at 02:15 in staging. Anyone oncall? :grimacing:
Michael L: assigning to Derek, Kim — can you pull the audit logs and KMS grant history? Ticket in SNYK-1234
Derek P: looking. quick question — is this the snapshot that had the new lifecycle policy applied? I see object key: tenant-42/snap-2026-03-21.tar.gz
Kim S: pulling CloudTrail and our object-store audit. Also checking IP/assume-role events. Will paste findings.
Kim S: CloudTrail shows PutObject by backup-uploader-sa at 02:15:12 with x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256, no x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id header. But snapshot metadata includes cmk_id:null
Anna R: So it's SSE-S3, not SSE-KMS. How did backup-agent decide that? We pushed RBAC change friday to restrict backup-agent IAM to put with cmk only.
Michael L: That suggests agent used a different service account or fallback path. Derek — could the uploader rotated keys and fell back to default SSE?
Derek P: Checking backup-agent logs... found sequence: `backup-agent: start upload`, then `upload: PutObject failed (AccessDenied: not authorized for kms:Encrypt)`, then `retry with SSE-S3`. ugh.
Anna R: Ok this is a vuln triage item — agent had access removed to kms:Encrypt but still could write object without kms, resulting in unencrypted-by-cmk snapshot persisted. Need rollback/hotfix.
Derek P: For immediate mitigation: 1) Quarantine the object (copy to quarantine-bucket with CMK re-encrypt?), 2) Revoke public access, 3) Rotate uploader keys.
Kim S: Copying object while re-encrypting via KMS requires access to plaintext or a server-side reencrypt. We can do `aws s3 cp s3://prodbucket/... s3://quarantine/... --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:...` but that needs s3:GetObject and kms:Encrypt on quarantine key.
Michael L: Also need audit trail: who changed IAM for backup-agent? I see a change 03/20 by infra-deployer: removed kms:Encrypt from backup-uploader-sa. tagging this to incident response.
ir-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042, priority P2. Assigned: Derek, Kim. Playbook: encrypt-at-rest-unexpected-snapshots.
Anna R: Action items: (A) restore kms:Encrypt for uploader with condition `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id` if possible, (B) add preventative test in preflight that validates PUT has kms headers, (C) audit historical objects for SSE-KMS tag missing.
Derek P: I'll do quarantine copy and rotate agent keys. Kim — can you run query: `select key from object_metadata where cmk_id is null and prefix like 'tenant-%' and created> '2026-03-01'` and return sample list?
Kim S: running. Found 4 objects in prod and 1 in staging. sending list in DMs. The oldest is tenant-9/snap-2026-03-05.tar.gz
Michael L: We'll need customer notification plan if any customer data impacted. Legal on call? @Anna please coordinate.
Anna R: Looping legal + customer-safety. Also adding an RBAC rollback for Friday's change — pin in PR to revert until preflight test exists.
Derek P: After quarantine, we'll run restore test to verify decrypt works with CMK and then delete original. No data exfil observed in logs so far.
Anna R: Good. One more: add CloudTrail log filter alert for PutObject that lacks SSE-KMS header for backup-buckets. Low cost rule.
Michael L: Agreed. I'll file ops ticket and rollout alert. Thanks team :thumbsup: 
Kim S: FYI after reencrypting to quarantine with CMK, kms:Decrypt logs show no external principals used.
Derek P: Closing loop: rotated keys, updated RBAC, added preflight test in ci. Will update INC-2026-042 with remediation timeline.
Anna R: Thanks everyone. Keep updates in thread. :lock:
